coverage_limits: Positive tests exercise static-channel RDPEFS announce/name/capability/device-list traffic with an empty redirected scratch folder; no file read/write operations are performed.

Upstream positive cases do not explicitly assert compression flags or chunk-size boundaries, and ignore DecodeClientPdu return values. Their original assertions are preserved; these are protocol exchange smoke tests, not full compression or filesystem conformance.
Negative TPKT/MCS length cases preserve the original malformed packet and disconnect assertions.
evidence_policy: Raw driver/client logs, exact-name TRX and bridge events retained. Temporary certificates, private keys, copied suites and binaries omitted.

excluded.reason: Requires Standard RDP Security signature fields; the current TLS profile does not exercise these fields and the Microsoft case returns before launching a client.

Fails original connection-drop expectation with strict driver verification in both modes. Client remains connected until cleanup; previous upstream apparent pass could be caused by ordinary traffic or a decoder exception.

disconnect_verification.defect: ExpectDisconnect throws InvalidOperationException for ordinary ReceivedPacket events or decoder exceptions, and WaitForDisconnection catches any such exception as true.
disconnect_verification.repair: Wait to the original bounded deadline, buffering ordinary packets; accept only a matching Disconnected event. Do not swallow InvalidOperationException. TLS receive EOF and IO errors including resets already emit Disconnected events in the upstream transport.
disconnect_verification.regression_evidence: With the original verifier the drive InvalidTPKTLength passed, but it fails the original assertion in both strict runs. InvalidMCSLength still passes with actual client disconnect. Both GFX capability negatives fail with strict verification.
